items.prompt: Rarely ___ such a talented young player.

explanation.en: Rarely at the start of the sentence needs question word order: auxiliary + subject.

optionNotes.en: Correct: inversion after rarely.
Normal word order is not possible after a fronted rarely.
Without an auxiliary, inversion needs did: rarely did I see.

items.prompt: Not until the results were published ___ how close the vote had been.

explanation.en: After a clause beginning Not until, the main clause is inverted with did.

optionNotes.en: Normal word order is not possible after Not until at the start.
Correct: did + subject + infinitive.
English inverts with an auxiliary, not by moving the main verb.

items.prompt: Hardly had she started speaking ___ the microphone stopped working.

explanation.en: Hardly is followed by when; than goes with no sooner.

optionNotes.en: Than goes with no sooner, not with hardly.
Correct: hardly… when.
That does not introduce the second event in this pattern.

items.prompt: No sooner had the film started ___ the power went off.

explanation.en: No sooner is followed by than.

optionNotes.en: When goes with hardly or scarcely, not with no sooner.
Correct: no sooner… than.
Then is an adverb of time, not part of this pattern.

items.prompt: Little ___ that their conversation was being recorded.

explanation.en: Little at the start means not at all, and it takes did + subject + verb.

optionNotes.en: Correct: inversion after little.
Normal word order is not possible after a fronted little.
Emphatic did must come before the subject here.

items.prompt: Only when you have read the whole contract ___ sign it.

explanation.en: After a clause beginning Only when, the main clause is inverted.

optionNotes.en: Normal word order is not possible after Only when at the start.
Correct: should + subject + verb.
This keeps normal word order, and shall sounds wrong here.

items.prompt: At no time ___ in any danger, according to the airline.

explanation.en: At no time is a negative expression, so the verb be comes before the subject.

optionNotes.en: Correct: inversion with be.
Normal word order is not possible after at no time.
This keeps normal word order and also drops the article.

items.prompt: So difficult ___ that only half the candidates passed.

explanation.en: So + adjective at the start for emphasis takes inversion: So difficult was the exam that…

optionNotes.en: Correct: so + adjective + be + subject.
After a fronted so + adjective, normal word order is not possible.
The extra pronoun it makes the sentence ungrammatical.
